subject: history_social
passage: Cyclists in Dutch cities often leave their bicycles on sidewalks near train stations, blocking pedestrians. In early 2020, one midsize Dutch city opened a large new bicycle garage beside its main station. Critics predicted that the garage would simply attract more cyclists while doing little about the clutter outside. City official Sanne de Vries argues, however, that the garage mainly drew bicycles off the sidewalks: most of the bikes parked in the garage, she says, would otherwise have been left outside.

data.title: Average Daily Bicycles Parked near a Dutch City's Main Station

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support de Vries's argument?

choices.A: From 2019 to 2020, sidewalk parking fell by about 2,500 bikes, while garage parking rose by about 3,000.
choices.B: Garage parking rose by far more than sidewalk parking fell, so the total number of parked bikes nearly doubled.
choices.C: In every year shown, more bicycles were parked in station garages than on the sidewalks.
choices.D: The number of bicycles parked on sidewalks changed little between 2020 and 2021.

explanation.why: De Vries claims that the new garage mostly moved bikes from the sidewalks rather than adding new ones. Support must compare the drop in sidewalk parking with the rise in garage parking when the garage opened. Sidewalk parking fell by about 2,500 while garage parking rose by about 3,000, so most of the garage's gain matches the sidewalks' loss.
explanation.A: Correct. The fall in sidewalk parking nearly equals the rise in garage parking, so most bikes in the new garage would otherwise have been on the sidewalks.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The total rose only from about 12,100 to 12,600 bikes, not nearly doubling, so this misreads the graph.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true, but it was also true before the new garage opened, so it says nothing about where the garage's bikes came from.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is true, but it describes the year after the opening and does not compare the sidewalk drop with the garage gain.
